{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"The branch came down more easily than Mara expected. She laid it beside the path and gathered the smaller cuttings, careful not to tread on the apples her mother had missed. One, no bigger than a walnut, had fallen into the hollow between two roots.

Inside, her mother stood at the sink with her sleeves rolled up. She turned each apple beneath the tap, setting the sound ones on a towel and the bruised ones in a bowl.

“There’s a recipe somewhere,” she said. “For a cake he used to make.”

“Grandad baked?”

“Only that cake. He said the trick was leaving the skins on.” Her mother shut off the tap. “I wrote it down after he died. I couldn’t find it when you were little.”

Mara set the shears on the draining board. For years, her mother had spoken of him in short, finished sentences: where he had worked, when he had left, the date of his funeral. Mara had learned not to ask what came between.

“We could look for it,” she said.

Her mother glanced toward the cupboard above the fridge. “I think it might be in the blue tin.”

Mara fetched a chair. The tin held old receipts, a photograph of a dog she didn’t recognize, and several folded sheets of paper. At the bottom lay a small card, its edges soft from handling. Her mother took it and read the ingredients aloud, pausing over the last line.

“What does it say?” Mara asked.

Her mother smiled a little. “Bake until the kitchen smells right.”"}
